title: AI World Simulator in the Browser — Aliveville
description: Play a real AI world simulator free in your browser. Aliveville runs autonomous NPCs with memory, relationships, and grudges in a persistent 3D town — no install.
summary: Paused AI world experiment with autonomous villagers. Hosted game offline; source available to run locally.

text.ai_world_simulator_covers_a_few: “AI world simulator” covers a few different products. An honest map of the space:
text.a_3d_town_of_autonomous_agents:
— a 3D town of autonomous agents with memory, playable free in the
          browser. Small, persistent, and open-source.
text.describe_a_world_in_text_and:
— describe a world in text and it
          generates a playable scenario around it. Generative breadth rather than one persistent town.
text.a_narrator_that_responds_to_your:
— a narrator that responds to your prompts.
          Flexible storytelling, but the world only moves when you type.
text.simulators_built_to_train_and_evaluate:
— simulators built to train and
          evaluate agents at scale. Powerful, but aimed at researchers with an engine install, not at
          players.
text.players_who_want_an_ai_civilization:
Players who want an AI civilization / life-sim sandbox; builders studying agent memory and
        multi-agent social loops; anyone comparing “AI world simulator” products that claim autonomous
        NPCs rather than single-player chat skins.

text.aliveville_is_an_early_opinionated_simul:
Aliveville is an early, opinionated simulator — not a full MMORPG or a research benchmark suite.
        Agent count, world size, and dialogue quality are bounded by the public browser build. Claims
        about “living AI people” mean autonomous simulation loops with memory, not general intelligence.
